primary_validator.description: reject_unapproved_paths always returns 404, regardless of method/credential -- this deployment's allowlist boundary.

rows.disclosure_behavior: Always 404, uniform for every unregistered path/method on this deployment.

primary_validator.description: require_admin (router-level dependency on admin.router:39-43, applies to every nested sub-router included after it) requires current_user.is_admin via get_current_user.

reachable_validators.description: OrgIdMiddleware.__call__ decodes the Authorization: Bearer value as an ops access-token JWT and resolves/validates X-Org-Id against it -- this IS the route's intended validator for ops_access_token_hs256.

ImpersonationMiddleware._may_be_superuser peeks at the Authorization bearer value with an UNVERIFIED base64 JSON decode of the JWT payload segment (token.split('.')[1]) on every request, superuser-or-not, with NO path exemption (unlike OrgIdMiddleware's /api/v1/internal/acr/ carve-out) -- runs even for ACR-authenticated requests. A non-JWT opaque token (svc_acr_*, fcpush_*, worker-bridge secret) fails the split/decode and is caught by a broad except, so this is benign but still 'observes' every credential class before its intended validator.

reachable_validators.description: OrgIdMiddleware.__call__ decodes the Authorization: Bearer value as an ops access-token JWT and resolves/validates X-Org-Id against it -- this IS the route's intended validator for ops_access_token_hs256.

ImpersonationMiddleware._may_be_superuser peeks at the Authorization bearer value with an UNVERIFIED base64 JSON decode of the JWT payload segment (token.split('.')[1]) on every request, superuser-or-not, with NO path exemption (unlike OrgIdMiddleware's /api/v1/internal/acr/ carve-out) -- runs even for ACR-authenticated requests. A non-JWT opaque token (svc_acr_*, fcpush_*, worker-bridge secret) fails the split/decode and is caught by a broad except, so this is benign but still 'observes' every credential class before its intended validator.

primary_validator.description: authorize_worker_bridge() (shared helper) checks Authorization: Bearer against WORKER_OPERATIONAL_BRIDGE_TOKEN with hmac.compare_digest + bounded length; fails closed (401) if unset. A repair-token route additionally rejects the value if it equals the ordinary bridge token, so bridge and repair capabilities can't be confused.

reachable_validators.description: OrgIdMiddleware.__call__ runs get_authenticated_user_from_headers on ANY Authorization header value, decoding it as an ops JWT via authenticate_access_token, before this route's own validator runs. Exempts only path prefix /api/v1/internal/acr/. A non-JWT bearer degrades to anonymous (InvalidTokenError caught, returns None) rather than erroring -- observable but not fatal.

ImpersonationMiddleware._may_be_superuser peeks at the Authorization bearer value with an UNVERIFIED base64 JSON decode of the JWT payload segment (token.split('.')[1]) on every request, superuser-or-not, with NO path exemption (unlike OrgIdMiddleware's /api/v1/internal/acr/ carve-out) -- runs even for ACR-authenticated requests. A non-JWT opaque token (svc_acr_*, fcpush_*, worker-bridge secret) fails the split/decode and is caught by a broad except, so this is benign but still 'observes' every credential class before its intended validator.

primary_validator.description: get_org_id: requires get_current_user (401 if the caller has no valid access token). The acting org is resolved from the X-Org-Id header, falling back to the caller's own JWT org, and is only returned if it equals the caller's own org, the caller has a Membership row for it, or the caller is a superuser; any other org id is rejected with 403 and no service call runs. While an impersonation session is active, the effective identity is the impersonation target and only the target's own org is reachable -- the superuser bypass does not apply.

A non-JWT opaque token (svc_acr_*, fcpush_*, worker-bridge secret) fails the split/decode and is caught by a broad except, so this is benign but still 'observes' every credential class before its intended validator.

anchor.note: _may_be_superuser unverified JWT peek, no path exemption

gaps: GraphQL resolver credential/action classification not individually re-derived per field in this pass (58 resolvers); every resolver runs inside the same Strawberry context built once per HTTP/WS request via context.py, which requires an authenticated ops_access_token_hs256 session (get_current_user-equivalent) before any resolver executes -- see docs/reference/auth/endpoint-profiles.md GraphQL section. Per-field/mutation entitlement + resource-resolver scoping not enumerated.

primary_validator.description: GraphQLContext.__post_init__ raises AuthorizationError unless org_id is set (or the user is a superuser); org_id is only ever populated from OrgIdMiddleware's validated-JWT+membership contextvar, so an unauthenticated/anonymous request has no path to a usable context.
